learning_outcomes.text: The student learns the reasons for the emergence of theories related to location selection.
The student gains the ability to think critically about the adequacy and applicability of location selection theories under current conditions.
The student learns basic approaches and analysis methods to understand the economic structure of cities.
Calculates location selection cost according to different variables.
Learns the basic laws related to rent formation.

syllabus_topics: Introduction: Economic system and market mechanism
Movement and interaction in economic space: Gravity theory
Impact of production components on location selection
The role of demand and scale in location selection: Agglomerations and externalities
Contemporary approaches in location selection: behavioral location theory
Midterm (Excuse) exam; Contemporary approaches in location selection: product life cycle theory
bibliography: Dicken, P. ve Lloyd, P.E. (1990), Location in Space: Theoretical Perspectives in Economic Geography, HarperCollins Publishers, New York.
